title: factdiff anchor --file takes either path form and proposes each fact's quote
goal: factdiff.py anchor --file accepts a path under kb/<root>/ as well as a root-relative one; a --quotes CSV may give a quote per cited source of a fact, as gate g1 decides; anchor --file F --propose prints, for each fact of F with no anchor row, the passage of each cited page that best holds it as a quote CSV line, writing nothing; anchoring one file rewrites no _anchors.csv or _fetch_state.csv row of another topic; the anchor part of test_live_kb.py proves each on a planted article (no new test id)

run: import subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/factdiff.py','anchor','--file','kb/public/security/zsh-completion-system.md','--dry-run'],capture_output=True,text=True);print((p.stdout+p.stderr)[-300:]);sys.exit(0 if p.returncode==0 and 'No file' not in p.stdout+p.stderr else 1)
import subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/factdiff.py','anchor','--help'],capture_output=True,text=True);sys.exit(0 if p.returncode==0 and '--propose' in p.stdout else 1)

gates.question: How does a --quotes CSV give one quote for each source a multi-source fact cites?
options: an optional source column (line,source,quote), two-column files read as before
several quotes in one cell joined by ' | ', matched to the cited sources in order
none: a multi-source fact is split into one bullet per source before anchoring
gates.recommendation: an optional source column (line,source,quote), two-column files read as before
gates.answer: an optional source column (line,source,quote), two-column files read as before

gates.question: Which facts of F does anchor --file F --propose print a quote line for?
options: each fact whose cited source holds no located anchor row for it: no row, or an unlocated one (no-match, fetch-error, not-text, gone)
only a fact with no anchor row at all
gates.recommendation: each fact whose cited source holds no located anchor row for it: no row, or an unlocated one (no-match, fetch-error, not-text, gone)
gates.answer: each fact whose cited source holds no located anchor row for it: no row, or an unlocated one (no-match, fetch-error, not-text, gone)

gates.question: Does --propose offer a passage below the anchoring cut for a fact the plain rule leaves unlocated?
options: yes: the page's best window when it shares at least 2 of the fact's terms, so a fact the cut leaves unlocated still gets a candidate quote to check
no: only a passage the plain anchoring rule would locate
gates.recommendation: yes: the page's best window when it shares at least 2 of the fact's terms, so a fact the cut leaves unlocated still gets a candidate quote to check
gates.answer: yes: the page's best window when it shares at least 2 of the fact's terms, so a fact the cut leaves unlocated still gets a candidate quote to check

gates.question: What shape does anchor --file F --propose print?
options: stdout: a header line,source,quote then one CSV line per fact and cited page, sorted by line; stderr: a counts line and one line per fact or page with no passage; exit 0; exit 2 for a missing or multiple --file or a combined selector or --quotes
stdout: two-column line,quote lines with no source
gates.recommendation: stdout: a header line,source,quote then one CSV line per fact and cited page, sorted by line; stderr: a counts line and one line per fact or page with no passage; exit 0; exit 2 for a missing or multiple --file or a combined selector or --quotes
